speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here because of acute diarrhea; to determine the cause, please tell me how many times you have had loose stools in the last 24 hours and if you have experienced any fever or blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). The patient is on levofloxacin and presents with frequent watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping, which is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. I will confirm this with a stool test for C. difficile toxins.
